q: My parents have told my husband and I repeatedly how they think it's so smart we are waiting longer to have a 2nd kid so that we can really enjoy the time with our firstborn... Well, now my oldest will only be around 2.5 when baby arrives.
cx: Nine weeks with an unexpected second; nobody but her partner knows yet.

q: I'm also due in January and my mom recently told me how happy she is I didn't tell her I was pregnant last month because "ick, a January baby would be awful" 😞
cx: Same author, dreading telling her parents.

q: I have already seen her a few times in the last few weeks and she has point blank asked me if I'm pregnant (IE, I don't want a drink, "Pregnant?!") to which I have to deflect pretty lamely.
cx: Same author on a close friend struggling to conceive a second.

q: Today my partner (aka the father of my child) told me he doesn’t want to know when appointments are, that he doesn’t want any decision making roles and that everything is up to me because “change is hard” for him.
cx: First-time mother at almost 9 weeks, unplanned, together since March; not living together.

q: I ended up confiding in his sister who told me “well you do talk about the pregnancy quite a bit” and I was very hurt. Both know my family is 26 hours away and in a different time zone
cx: Same author; her own family is supportive but far away.

q: It’s almost making me stress about big conversations that have to happen (aka is my partner going to move in, am I looking at buying a house somewhere, what is my mat leave going to be, financially where do we stand, does my partner want to be in this as coparents or a couple etc).
cx: Same author, the night before a licensing exam.

q: My coordinator had been helping me navigate this “unexplained hostility” for going on 3 weeks of this treatment, and finally today I found out that she had told my leadership that I’m pregnant.
cx: Paid internship; she had told HR and her coordinator, not her boss.

q: I told my HR before I even told my coordinator, and told her I didn’t feel comfortable telling my boss until I returned to work, which HR fully supported and even said that technically I could have more time than that if I wanted, I only needed to give 1 month heads up for needed paperwork and getting in my leave.
cx: Same author; what HR told her about timing.

q: I could have foreseen this response and would have declined any special treatment if I knew, especially with pregnancy as a reason. I’ve witnessed and heard of too many convenient layoffs to want to give them any ammo.
cx: Same author; the coordinator asked for reduced travel on her behalf.

q: your milk can take 3-5 days to come in. It initially hurts and your boobs become hard and engorged with milk. I didn’t even know that was a thing and it can be shocking if you’ve never heard of it.
cx: Second-time mother and paramedic writing a list of what she wished she'd known.

q: I did tons of research on unmedicated births leading up to my first and second births, but all the techniques necessitated movement (which I wasn’t allowed) or a birthing tub, so I felt totally unprepared. I also did hypnobirthing but that was kind of a flop for me.
cx: Pregnant with her third, hoping to labour without pain relief this time.

q: Yes I’ve listened to tons of birth stories, did hypnobirthing classes, and attempted to get a doula with my first, but my insurance totally bungled its doula program so I couldn’t get anyone.
cx: Same author on what she tried before.

q: I’m just thinking if I get a doula but I’m not allowed to move, is it even worth it?
cx: Same author weighing a doula for the third birth.

q: I’m hoping to avoid induction this time around although now that I’m 35 I’m sure they’ll be pushing for it, especially since my last baby was 10 lbs.
I’m not sure how much she will have to say since she only shows up for the last 5 minutes and actually missed the birth last time
cx: Same author on raising her plan with the provider.

q: had my first baby 7 years ago and am pregnant with my second (only 5w), and although the life conditions the first time around were way more stressful and uncertain, somehow this time I’m SO much more anxious?!
cx: Second pregnancy seven years after the first.

q: Me my husband and 7yo have such a lovely calm life, our son loves museums and we spend our weekends learning about history and hanging out (and sleeping in!) and I’m so scared of upsetting the balance, even though he has begged for a sibling for years.
I think my worry is what if it doesn’t complete on time ! X
cx: 20 weeks; just sold their flat and want to buy a house before the baby.

q: the doctor who did the blood draw told me that bad news come by phone, good news in an email.
cx: Waiting on an early screening blood test, already very anxious.
